# NIST DLMF — Complex Variable and Conformal Mapping (2026)

## Chicago 18 forms

**Full note:** F. W. J. Olver et al., *NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions*, release 1.2.7 (National Institute of Standards and Technology, 2026), §1.9(iv), https://dlmf.nist.gov/1.9.iv.

**Shortened note:** NIST DLMF, §1.9(iv).

**Bibliography:** Olver, F. W. J., Daniel W. Lozier, Ronald F. Boisvert, and Charles W. Clark, eds. *NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions*. Release 1.2.7, 2026. National Institute of Standards and Technology. §1.9(iv). https://dlmf.nist.gov/1.9.iv.

## Essay use

NIST DLMF establishes a narrow complex-analysis formulation: the extended complex plane adds an ideal infinity point, and cross-ratio invariance stated there is under bilinear transformations. It keeps §3/#3 technically exact while refusing a general inference from completion to QL.

**Claim boundary:** it does not establish real-projective parallel-line geometry, invariance under every transformation, a universal rule of dimensional reframing, or any QL, Buddhist, or metaphysical conclusion.

## Passage card — `nist-dlmf-2026-complex-variable-q001` — extended complex plane
^nist-dlmf-2026-complex-variable-q001

> “The extended complex plane, \(\widehat{\mathbb C}\), consists of the points of the complex plane together with an ideal point called the point at infinity.”

- **Locator:** §1.9(iv), opening paragraph immediately before Eq. 1.9.35.
- **Status:** quotation-ready.
- **Verification:** Luna acquisition agent and coordinator, 2026-07-14; manual transcription checked against NIST HTML; OCR uncertainty: none.
- **Source relation:** extracted.
- **Evidential action:** supports.
- **Argument function:** technical/formal warrant.
- **Consumers:** [[28-s3-p3-projective-dimensional-reframing]]; [Core Theorem Bridge](../../../../../eight-determinations.md); [[section-rooms/arguments/A17-Toroidal-Circulation-and-the-Arche-Topos|Toroidal Circulation and the Arche-Topos]]; movement 28 complex completion.
- **Use boundary:** establishes a specified complex-plane completion only; it does not establish real-projective geometry, QL, or a metaphysical interpretation of infinity.

<a id="nist-dlmf-2026-complex-variable-q002"></a>
## Passage card — `nist-dlmf-2026-complex-variable-q002` — cross-ratio scope
^nist-dlmf-2026-complex-variable-q002

> “The cross ratio … is invariant under bilinear transformations.”

- **Locator:** §1.9(iv), “Bilinear Transformation,” text immediately after Eq. 1.9.45.
- **Status:** quotation-ready.
- **Verification:** Luna acquisition agent and coordinator, 2026-07-14; manual transcription checked against NIST HTML and permanent Eq. 1.9.45 locator; OCR uncertainty: none.
- **Source relation:** extracted.
- **Evidential action:** qualifies.
- **Argument function:** technical scope limitation.
- **Consumers:** [[28-s3-p3-projective-dimensional-reframing]]; [Core Theorem Bridge](../../../../../eight-determinations.md); [[section-rooms/arguments/A17-Toroidal-Circulation-and-the-Arche-Topos|Toroidal Circulation and the Arche-Topos]]; movement 28 cross-ratio boundary.
- **Use boundary:** limits the stated invariance to bilinear transformations; it does not support a claim that all transformations preserve cross-ratio or that mathematical invariance establishes QL.
